title: NATS request/reply pipelines.providers.key.write (studio → pipelines)
description: From API 1.52 (plan 27). Core NATS request/reply on subject `pipelines.providers.key.write` (queue group `pipelines`), bare JSON, for PUT and DELETE /v1/studio/admin/provider-keys/{key_secret}. The only message that carries a provider key: the subject is core request/reply only and must never be added to a JetStream stream (nothing stores, replays or dead-letters it); only the studio user may publish it and only pipelines subscribe (nats.conf). `save`: unless `force`, pipelines lists `GET <provider.base_url>/models` with the key in memory (the host rule and the remote switch, 15 s; the snapshot comes from a preset or a saved provider, never the browser); 401 or 403 is `refused`, anything else that is not an answer `unreachable`; nothing is written then. With an answer (`ok`) or `force` (`skipped`) the key, trimmed, is written into the first key folder (PIPELINES_PROVIDER_KEYS_DIR) only, by a temp file and rename, mode 0600. `remove`: the first folder's file of that name is deleted (missing is fine). The reply never holds the key, and `detail` is our own fixed text, never the provider's body. Studio waits 30 s for save, 5 s for remove (no answer: 503).

key.description: the key, trimmed: printable ASCII without spaces

provider.description: the provider the key is checked with (a providerSnapshot without key_secret)

force.description: Save anyway: write without a call

found.description: after it: a regular file of that name, not empty, in one of the key folders

detail.description: refused or unreachable: our own short text

code.description: readonly: the first key folder is not writable; not_file: a folder of that name is there
